description: Step 1 of the §6.8 Habiro experiment: verifies Family-A q-dim identity, maps the Σ_{λ⊢n} dim_q family, and shows the figure-eight Habiro element diverges at real q₀ (so Family-A must be the PERTURBATIVE Habiro series, not the convergent sum). EXPLORATORY; no production path touched.

part2_dim_q_family.note: Family-A uses n=4 with normalization 1/4: (1/4)Σ_{λ⊢4} = 5/2 + (3/4)h². The table below maps the analogous Σ_{λ⊢n} for n=3..6 so the per-knot selection rule (which n, which normalization) can be compared against Φ_K once external coefficients land.

part3_figure_eight_habiro.divergence_mechanism: |(1−q^j)(1−q^{-j})| = q^j + q^{-j} − 2 ~ q^j for q>1, so ∏_{j=1}^n ~ q^{n(n+1)/2} — super-exponential, the SAME growth that refuted the α_r single-rank q-Pochhammer ansatz (docs/audits/...alpha-r...). The naive Habiro sum is NOT summable at real q₀>1 — but it is an ASYMPTOTIC series: least-term truncation at n_opt gives a finite Borel-sum estimate.
part3_figure_eight_habiro.implication: The framework's FINITE linking_weight (5/2 + 3h²/4) cannot be the convergent Habiro sum at q₀. It must be the PERTURBATIVE / asymptotic series of the Habiro element around q=1 (the Garoufalidis–Zagier Φ_K(h) formal series), evaluated as a truncated polynomial in h. The G-S-W-Z 2024 resummation (Borel / K_3-graded) is what assigns a finite value to the divergent sum — exactly the resurgence content the §6.8 experiment needs.

part3b_trefoil_control.note: Non-hyperbolic control. A Vol-driven plateau interpretation of the figure-eight Part-3 result predicts qualitatively different behaviour here (no geometric saddle).

If the h² coefficients match — the Geom_full bridge is DERIVED from the Habiro element, not fit. K_3 grading makes the coefficients rigid (no free params).
